--- title: "[Graph.add_reverse_edges_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add reverse edges for all selected edges (directed graphs only). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L31979-L32107){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_reverse_edges_ws(**edge_attributes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Add reverse edges for the selection](/assets/graphs/add-reverse-edges-ws.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a directed six-node graph with edges B→C and D→E selected in the accent color. Right: each selected edge gains a reverse partner, C→B and E→D, drawn in the accent color; the original edges stay, so those pairs now point both ways." width="100%"} For each selected edge (A->B), adds the reverse edge (B->A) if it doesn't already exist. Useful for making directed graphs bidirectional or adding reciprocal relationships. The method works on the current edge selection (the `_ws` suffix means "with selection"), so it is usually chained after `select_edges()` or `select_edges_by_id()`. Node selections are ignored. The original edges are kept, the graph is modified in place, and the selection is left as it was (the new reverse edges are not added to it). Typical uses: - marking certain relationships as mutual, such as reciprocal friendships or binding interactions that work both ways - making part of a directed graph two-way while leaving the rest one-way - preparing a directed graph for an algorithm that needs paths in both directions The reverse edges are new edges: they do not copy the weight or attributes of the edge they mirror. Pass those values through `**edge_attributes` if the reverse edges need them. When a reverse edge is already present, nothing is added for that pair and the existing edge is not changed. To flip edges rather than mirror them, use `rev_edge_dir_ws()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [**edge_attributes]{.doc-parameter-name} : Optional attributes to set on the newly created reverse edges, passed through to `add_edge()`, for example `weight=1.0` or `kind="reciprocal"`. The same values are applied to every new edge. With no keyword arguments, the new edges have no weight and no attributes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~rev_edge_dir_ws`) : Reverse the direction of the selected edges instead. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting the single edge `A->B` and adding its reverse gives two edges, one in each direction: ::: {#196364cf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label='A') .add_node(label='B') .add_edge(source='A', target='B', weight=1.0) ) # Add reverse edge edge_ids = list(graph.get_edge_ids()) ( graph .select_edges_by_id([edge_ids[0]]) .add_reverse_edges_ws(weight=1.0) ) graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['A->B', 'B->A'] ``` ::: ::: Make selected edges bidirectional -- here, only the heavier "A->B" edge gets a reverse, since "B->C" falls below the weight threshold. That leaves three edges: ::: {#cb284725 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(['A', 'B', 'C']) .add_edges([('A', 'B', 10.0), ('B', 'C', 3.0)]) ) ( graph .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight is not None and e.weight > 5.0) .add_reverse_edges_ws() ) graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: The new `B->A` edge did not inherit the weight of `A->B`, because no `weight=` was passed: ::: {#5d91e6ee .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_df().select(["source", "target", "weight"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
